mappings.note: Iodine as the lustrous non-metal is the standard exception used when classifying by physical properties - LO-1, with no reaction or extraction content.
Selecting the metal that will not displace hydrogen from dilute acid is a below-hydrogen judgement on the activity series, so LO-2 rather than the general metal+acid property of LO-1.
Requires ordering Mg, Zn, Cu and Ag and then predicting displacement from salt solution - the exact predictive use named in LO-2.
Writes the equation for one named metal with water. The demand is the product of a single metal's reaction, not a comparison, so LO-1.

Gold is identified by resisting both concentrated acids and dissolving only in aqua regia, i.e. by sitting at the bottom of the series (LO-2). C 8.2 is cited because the item is an observation-to-inference task over three labelled test tubes; C 8.2-LO-2 is NOT used because the variable changed is the reagent, not the metal - only one metal is tested.
Equation for iron with steam - a single metal's reaction product, so LO-1, in contrast with items that rank iron against other metals.

WEAK FIT. The item classifies an alloy as a homogeneous mixture; that is mixture classification, which no outcome covers. LO-7 is cited because 'alloying' appears only there in the outcome layer. See the reported alloy gap.
Contrasts Na, K and Ca with 'most other metals' on the basis of electropositivity - a ranking of metals, so LO-2 rather than the single-metal chemical property of LO-1.
Electrode polarity in an electrolytic cell belongs to the refining stage of extraction, the only place the curriculum puts electrolysis (LO-6). It is not a corrosion or classification item.
Explicitly asks whether M is a metal or a non-metal, inferred from the basic character of its oxide - LO-1's classification demand in its purest form.
Where the pure metal deposits during electrolytic refining - the last step of LO-6's extraction sequence. No reactivity ranking is required.
Identifies copper from its own behaviour on heating in air and names the black oxide. One metal, one reaction, so LO-1 and not the series.

The knife-soft clue identifies the element as an alkali metal (LO-1 physical property), but separating Na from Ca, which also reacts with water, needs relative vigour (LO-2). Both are genuinely required; neither alone settles the answer.

Reads occurrence (combined vs free) back onto position in the activity series - explicitly an 'arranges metals in order of reactivity' inference, so LO-2 rather than the extraction outcome, since nothing is extracted here.
WEAK FIT. Alloy composition recall (carbon in steel). Assigned to LO-7 as the only outcome naming alloying; the item tests constituents, not corrosion resistance.
Asks directly for a metal/non-metal verdict from the acid-base character of two oxides - the chemical-property half of LO-1.

All four options concern magnesium alone across cold water, hot water and steam. The variable is the condition, not the metal, so this is a single-substance chemical property (LO-1), not a series item.
Names the product class of metal + hydrogen (hydrides) as a general chemical property of metals - LO-1. The sibling item about which metals form hydrides is LO-2 because it ranks them.
WEAK FIT. Amalgam composition recall; the mercury constituent is the whole demand. Cited to LO-7 only because alloying appears nowhere else in the outcome layer.
Colour and composition of the coating formed when copper is heated - one metal's reaction with oxygen. Distinct from the green-patina item, which is corrosion over time (LO-7).

Electron transfer forms an ionic compound whose properties must then be predicted. No learning outcome covers bond formation or ionic-compound properties, so the competency, which names compound formation from atomic structure and valency, is the closest legal code.
Zinc displacing copper from copper sulphate is the canonical displacement reaction predicted by the series - LO-2, even though the demand is the balanced equation.

The question asks which element is the metal and which the non-metal, so LO-1 is the demand. Note the outcome names physical and chemical properties as the basis, while this item works from electronic configuration - a wording shortfall recorded in the defect list.
Works from a given reactivity ordering to predict which metal occurs free - the reasoning is pure series reasoning (LO-2). LO-6 was rejected because no ore or extraction step is involved.
Picks the metal whose oxide breaks the 'metal oxides are basic' rule. Amphoterism is a chemical-property boundary case in the metal/non-metal classification, so LO-1.
